crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice uses AI to tailor portfolio construction to an individual's goals, constraints, tax situation, risk tolerance, and time horizon.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance moves past the Markowitz framework that uses only expected return and volatility.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in AI portfolio construction is the practice of reducing exposure to rare but severe losses that can hit concentrated AI equity, credit, or venture positions.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios refer to environmental, social and governance criteria used alongside financial metrics when selecting and weighting assets, including AI-related instruments.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers positions that do not trade on an active exchange, such as private AI company equity, venture fund interests, restricted stock, intellectual property, data rights, and thinly traded tokens.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of deciding what assets a portfolio should hold, in what amounts, and how those holdings should change as goals, markets, and constraints shift. Artificial intelligence now enters this work through data pipelines, risk models, and allocation engines that estimate returns, covariances, and exposures from large sets of market and alternative data. In personalised advice, systems build model portfolios from a client profile, then monitor drift and suggest rebalancing trades. In optimisation, machine learning and mathematical programming handle many assets, transaction costs, taxes, and constraints that simple mean and variance methods ignore. In tail risk hedging, models scan for regime changes and stress scenarios, then size hedges or adjust exposures. In sustainability and illiquid asset pricing, language models read disclosures and documents, while valuation models combine comparable sales, cash flow forecasts, and market signals.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has solved several practical steps, including data ingestion, risk factor calculation, constrained optimisation, and automated rebalancing, which now appear in production systems. The site tracks 117 listed AI related instruments with daily prices, which gives a usable universe for testing allocation ideas, though it is far smaller than the full investable market. What remains hard is personalisation that is genuinely useful rather than a thin questionnaire, because goals, tax situations, and risk capacity vary in ways that data rarely captures. Tail risk is not solved, since rare events are sparse in history and models often underestimate dependence when markets fall together. Sustainability factors are unsettled, because disclosures are inconsistent, ratings disagree, and the link from a factor to future returns is noisy. Pricing illiquid assets remains the weakest area, with few transactions, stale marks, and wide uncertainty bands, and all of these areas face overfitting, nonstationarity, model risk, limited explainability, and the need for human oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section form a chain from client needs to asset valuation. Personalised Wealth Advice is the entry point, covering how goals, risk tolerance, and suitability shape a starting allocation and ongoing recommendations. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance goes deeper into the mathematics and constraints that turn those preferences into weights across many assets. Tail Risk Hedging follows the allocation question into downside protection, regime detection, and stress testing for extreme markets. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios addresses how environmental, social, and governance data enter the same optimisation and reporting process. Pricing Illiquid Assets closes the chain by handling private, infrequent, or hard to value holdings that do not have clean daily prices. A reader would go to each page for its specific method, its data demands, and its known failure modes.
